THESE PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

A private complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C., was filed by the 2nd respondent under Sections 13(1)(c) (d) (e) r/w 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, under Sections 409, 420 r/w Section 34 of IPC alleging that, accused No.2 to 3 conniving with accused Nos.4 to 11, created the documents purportedly to show that the subject lands which are reserved as 'Gomala lands' belongs to them, and thereafter induced the Government to acquire the subject lands for Yagachi Hemavathi Reservoir project, and by using the said documents received compensation under the award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer, and also enhanced compensation from the Reference Court.

The learned Magistrate referred the compliant to the respondent-Lokyukta for investigation under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C.
2.

Mr. Ashok. S. Haranahalli, learned senior counsel and Mr. P.P. Hegde, learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioners-accused would submit that the offences alleged against the petitioners-accused are cognizable, and the private complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C., filed by the 2nd respondent without complying with Section 154(1) & 154(3) of Cr.P.C., and also not supported by an affidavit is not maintainable as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Priyanka Srivastava -vs- State of Uttar Pradesh and Others reported in (2015) 6 SCC 287.
Smt Ningamma @ Lakshmamma vs The State on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31415242/
4 3.

entities.text: Priyanka Srivastava -vs- State of Uttar Pradesh and Others reported in (2015) 6 SCC 287
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On the other hand, Mr. B.B. Patil, learned Spl.P.P., appearing for the respondent-Lokyukta submits that, the allegations made in the compliant discloses the commission of the cognizable offence, and the veracity of the allegations requires to be investigated, and at this stage, the registration of FIR does not warrant any interference and sought for dismissal of the petitions.
4. I have examined the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties.
5. Offences alleged against the petitioners-accused are cognizable.

Perusal of the complaint indicates that, except the averments that 2nd respondent approached the Lokayukta Police, and Lokayukta Police in turn stated that it has no jurisdiction to investigate the allegations, there are no specific allegations that, on the refusal to register the compliant by the officer in charge of the Police Station,
he approached the higher official to take appropriate action against the petitioners- accused.

The complaint was filed without complying with the mandatory provisions of Section 154(1) & 154(3) of Cr.P.C.
6.

Hence, the private complaint filed by the 2nd respondent without complying with the aforesaid provisions is not maintainable in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Priyanka Srivastava supra.
7.
In view of the preceding analysis, the continuation of investigation against the petitioners-accused will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The Criminal petitions are allowed ii) The impugned order dated 5.2.2018 passed by the Prl.District & Sessions Judge,
Hassan in PCR. No.1/2018 referring the complaint to the respondent No.1 for investigation under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C., is hereby quashed.
iii) Complaint stands dismissed as against petitioners herein.
iv) Liberty is reserved with the complainant to lodge a complaint afresh if,
permissible in law.
Sd/-
